title: General, predictive functionalization of a chosen unactivated C–H bond in a complex molecule

concept.text: The proposed innovation would let a chemist select an unactivated carbon–hydrogen bond within a complex molecule and predictably transform that site while preserving the molecule’s other useful features. The central challenge is choosing among competing C–H bonds and functional groups: the desired reaction must occur at the selected position, avoid unwanted transformations elsewhere, and control stereochemistry where it matters. The supplied reviews establish the importance of site predictability and chemoselectivity, but do not demonstrate this full proposed capability.

Conceptual scope: the desired capability is general chemical control of a selected bond transformation, potentially delivered by a family of catalysts and predictive selection rules rather than one catalyst. Unactivated C(sp3)–H bonds are a central target. Aromatic C–H chemistry provides relevant context, but success at an aromatic site does not by itself demonstrate control over an unactivated C(sp3)–H site. Demonstrating one stated transformation would establish a narrower capability than installing any desired group at any chosen position.

significance.text: Predictable access to a selected C–H bond would expand synthetic planning. Chemists could plan routes around converting a bond already present in a carbon skeleton into a new functional connection, creating additional retrosynthetic disconnections and potentially avoiding some pre-functionalization steps. The 2025 review identifies streamlined, atom-economical synthesis from simpler starting materials as a benefit of C(sp3)–H functionalization. Extending that benefit reliably to chemist-selected sites in complex molecules is the revolutionary prospect.

More flexible late-stage diversification could allow an existing complex molecule to serve as the starting point for multiple derivatives, instead of requiring a substantially redesigned synthesis for each variant. Pharmaceutical and natural-product chemistry are plausible beneficiaries because the 2023 review explicitly discusses direct functionalization of these complex targets. Shorter routes and easier exploration of molecular variants remain conditional benefits: they depend on useful yields, accessible reagents, functional-group tolerance, stereochemical control and practical reaction conditions.

Impact synthesis: routine diversification across drugs and natural products would require substantially broader validation than success with one transformation on one test panel. A useful method might shorten some routes while offering little advantage for others. This concept does not require a single catalyst that replaces every enzyme or also solves methane oxidation; those are separate capabilities with additional constraints.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability targeted here is reliable, prospective control over which unactivated C–H bond reacts in a crowded molecular environment. The 2023 review documents regioselectivity and chemoselectivity challenges as molecules acquire dense and diverse functional groups. It also identifies increasing risks of catalyst intolerance and limited applicability as functional groups and potentially Lewis-basic heteroatoms accumulate. A broadly useful method must therefore combine site selection with compatibility across the surrounding molecule, rather than solve either requirement in isolation.

The 2025 abstract describes non-directed activation, transiently directed activation and activation directed by native functionality, alongside photoredox catalysis and organocatalysis. These approaches provide different ways to obtain reactivity and selectivity. The engineering goal is to turn such capabilities into dependable instructions for a preselected site, with an explicit account of where each approach succeeds or fails. Their enumeration supports the existence of a varied toolkit; it does not prove that every approach is case-specific or that no sufficiently general method exists.

Synthesis of the remaining requirements: a convincing system would need to predict both the desired outcome and important competing outcomes before experimentation, deliver enough desired product to be useful, and control relevant stereochemistry. It would also need to define its operating limits, including acceptable reaction conditions and any substrate-specific preparation. These requirements describe the proposed breakthrough; the supplied abstracts neither establish that they have all been met nor establish their universal absence as of November 1, 2026.

current_state.text: The 2023 Chemical Reviews survey by Docherty, Larrosa and colleagues, reported in the supplied research as published June 28, 2023 in volume 123, pages 7692–7760, documents progress in direct metal-catalyzed C–C bond formation within complex targets. Its abstract specifically includes alkylation, methylation, arylation and olefination. This is evidence of substantial existing chemistry, alongside documented limits in regioselectivity, chemoselectivity and catalyst tolerance. The review concerns broader C–H chemistry, so its entire scope should not be treated as demonstrations of selected unactivated C(sp3)–H functionalization.

The 2025 Chemical Society Reviews article, “Unified approaches in transition metal catalyzed C(sp3)–H functionalization,” surveys photoredox catalysis, organocatalysis, non-directed C–H activation, transiently directed activation and native-functionality-directed activation. These are established research strategies described by a review, rather than a demonstration in the supplied material of one general reaction. The research gives January 22, 2025 as the publication date; the retained bibliographic alternative gives a February 17, 2025 issue date and volume 54(4), pages 2006–2053. The supplied material does not resolve the relationship between those dates.

The evidence available through the supplied review is partial. The 2023 PubMed record provided an abstract and figure captions; the full review and figures were not inspected. The source indexed under the ACS PDF URL actually retained a matching Manchester Research Explorer abstract page, so the earlier attribution to PDF section 1.1 is unverified. For the 2025 RSC article, the retained alternative was a matching PubMed abstract record. That record lists two corrections whose contents were unavailable, leaving their relevance to these conclusions undetermined.

Evidence boundary: the supplied review contains no freshness-search results assessing developments after these publications. It therefore supports dated descriptions of progress and challenges, rather than a comprehensive determination of the field on November 1, 2026. No quantitative demonstration of the full proposed capability is supplied. The earlier assertions about chain-walking limitations and strained metallacycles explaining difficult para-selective aromatic functionalization are not established by the retained texts; that evidence gap does not show that either assertion is false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed initial demonstration: evaluate a method prospectively on a blinded panel of polyfunctional molecules, each containing several competing unactivated C–H sites. Specify the target site and one stated transformation before testing. The selected site should be the major site of that transformation, common polar groups should be tolerated, and the process should avoid installing a permanent directing group. These are proposed benchmark choices, not established community standards; perfect selectivity is not required.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed initial demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reporting requirements: define panel composition, substrate-selection rules and success criteria in advance. Report desired-product yield, site selectivity, competing functional-group reactions, relevant stereochemical outcomes, failures and reaction conditions. A major-site result alone is insufficient if very little useful product forms. Disclose any temporary directing-group steps, reliance on native directing functionality, catalyst changes or substrate-specific optimization so that the practical burden and degree of predictability can be assessed.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reporting requirements

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and breadth requirements: independent laboratories should reproduce representative successes and limitations using the disclosed procedures. Testing should include several preselected positions on suitable individual molecules where feasible, as well as chemically diverse substrates, to distinguish selectable-site control from repeated exploitation of one favorable site class. Success would establish demonstrated breadth for the tested transformations and conditions. Broader claims about group installation, stereochemical control, scale or routine late-stage use would require additional demonstrations; finite testing cannot establish literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility and breadth requirements

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis — CHEMREV-01, “A method that predicts realistic chemical outcomes before the experiment”: predictive chemistry could help select catalysts and conditions for the target C–H bond and anticipate competing reactions. The distinction is between predicting an outcome and physically achieving the selected transformation. Accurate predictions of failure would advance CHEMREV-01 without completing CHEMREV-11.

Roster-based synthesis — CHEMREV-04, “Practical, on-demand synthesis of arbitrary stable molecules”: reliable selected-site functionalization could expand the reactions available to an automated or on-demand synthesis system. CHEMREV-11 concerns control of a particular bond transformation; CHEMREV-04 concerns the broader ability to make requested molecules, which also requires route planning and execution of other steps.

Roster-based synthesis — CHEMREV-05, “Enzyme-level catalysts on request for arbitrary reactions”: a catalyst designed on demand, potentially an enzyme, could be one implementation of selected-site C–H functionalization. CHEMREV-11 does not prescribe the catalyst type, and a successful implementation would not establish catalyst availability for arbitrary reactions. These comparisons use the supplied roster titles; full records for CHEMREV-04 and CHEMREV-05 were not supplied.

Roster-based synthesis — CHEMREV-12, “Selective conversion of methane to methanol at useful conversion under mild conditions”: both concepts involve selective C–H transformation. Their central selectivity problems differ. CHEMREV-11 targets a chosen position among competing sites in a complex molecule, whereas CHEMREV-12 targets a particular conversion of methane with useful conversion and mild conditions. Completion of either would not establish the other.

Roster-based synthesis — CHEMREV-10, “Positional chemical manufacture of macroscopic, atomically specified matter”: choosing a reaction site within a molecule has a conceptual connection to positional chemical control. CHEMREV-11 remains a molecular synthesis capability and would not demonstrate macroscopic manufacture of atomically specified structures.

change_log.change: Preserved CHEMREV-11 and its title while separating the broad selected-bond capability from a narrower demonstration of one transformation.
change_log.reason: The proposed benchmark cannot establish arbitrary group installation, universal substrate coverage or general stereochemical control.

change_log.change: Integrated the synthetic-planning benefits with explicit dependencies on yield, scope, stereochemistry and practical conditions.
change_log.reason: New disconnections and streamlined routes are grounded conditional benefits; routine diversification and a ranking of pharmaceutical routes as the leading near-term use are not established.

change_log.change: Removed the generalization that complex molecules are usually made through early functionalization followed by protection and deprotection.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence supports avoiding some pre-functionalization, but does not establish the prevalence claim.

change_log.change: Replaced catalyst-poisoning language with catalyst intolerance and retained the role of functional-group density and Lewis-basic heteroatoms.
change_log.reason: The abstract documents intolerance without establishing a specific poisoning mechanism.

change_log.change: Expanded the documented reaction and strategy lists and distinguished aromatic chemistry from unactivated C(sp3)–H functionalization.
change_log.reason: This preserves useful evidence detail without treating every reviewed reaction as a direct demonstration of the target capability.

change_log.change: Qualified claims about universal absence, chain-walking limitations and para-selectivity mechanisms.
change_log.reason: The retained abstracts do not establish those assertions, and the empty freshness record cannot support a comprehensive present-day conclusion.

change_log.change: Corrected the description of source access and preserved publication-date and correction-notice uncertainties.
change_log.reason: The retained alternatives were abstract records rather than the full reviews; the PDF section locator and contents of two corrections remain unavailable.

change_log.change: Developed the proposed benchmark with reporting, independent reproduction and practical-boundary requirements.
change_log.reason: Major-site selectivity alone would not demonstrate useful yield, predictable operation or broad applicability.

change_log.change: Used the supplied roster titles to explain overlaps with CHEMREV-01, CHEMREV-04, CHEMREV-05, CHEMREV-10 and CHEMREV-12.
change_log.reason: The roster supports conceptual comparisons, while the absence of full related records limits detailed cross-entry verification.

unresolved_issues: Developments after the supplied 2023 and 2025 reviews remain unassessed; the evidence does not determine whether the full capability exists as of November 1, 2026.
The contents and relevance of the two corrections listed for the 2025 review are unknown.
The relationship between the supplied January 22, 2025 publication date and the retained February 17, 2025 issue date is not resolved.
The ACS PDF section 1.1 locator, chain-walking limitations and proposed strained-metallacycle explanation for para-selectivity are not verified by the retained material.
The benchmark still requires concrete choices of transformation, substrate-panel breadth, acceptable yield and selectivity, stereochemical requirements, operating conditions and scale.
Full records for the related concepts were not supplied, so comparisons beyond their roster titles remain provisional.
